market_holds: Spot $8.11 at the 18:08 UTC seal (sealed baseline), market cap about $154M on 18.9M shares. The front-expiry (Nov 20) straddle implies about 16.3% for the event, but the ATM spread is 50% of mid and open interest is only 356 contracts, so treat it as indicative. Reactions over the last eight prints: median 4.9%, but the three 2026 full prints moved +33%, +18% and +21%, all on balance-sheet and turnaround news. The 2026-11-02 preliminary release (Q3 comps +3.9%, traffic -1.7%, check +5.6%, 108 restaurants sold for $89.4M, call delayed to Nov 18) drew -0.9%. The stock has since drifted from $9.24 (Nov 4) to $8.15: -9.5% over 5 days against IWM -4.4%, SPY -3.8%, and casual-dining peers up (BJRI +2.2%, EAT +0.2%, CAKE +7.6%, TXRH +1.2%, DIN +4.2%), per Yahoo bars. The mechanical cost of the refranchising has been public since the 2026-09-01 8-K pro forma: about $40.7M a year of EBITDA lost (on FY25), about $0.9M a week (on 28 weeks of 2026), and G&A not adjusted. The stock fell 7% on the day it was filed and kept falling from about $9.1 to $7.0 by Sept 21. Old FY26 guide (2026-08-12): adj EBITDA $70-73M, comps 0.5-1.5%, excluding the deals. Consensus is thin and stale: Benzinga shows Q3 EPS -$0.43 on $254M revenue, and other aggregators show older and conflicting figures. A Nov 11 MarketBeat snapshot gives a mean price target of about $8.33 (range $7-10). Short interest was 1.86M shares on Oct 30, about 9.8% of shares outstanding and about 10 days to cover (Nasdaq).
view: The release decides on the FY26 guide rebuilt for a franchise-heavier model, plus Q3 EBITDA. The headline numbers are not the line: Q2 missed EPS by 60% and the stock rose 21% on the refranchising news. My own arithmetic from the company's pro forma: H2 loses about $14-15M of EBITDA (about 5 weeks of Q3 and all of Q4 without 108 stores). Against the old $70-73M guide and the Q3 comps beat (+3.9% against a 0.5-1.5% full-year guide), that implies an updated FY26 adj EBITDA of roughly $56-60M. That figure is a clean number to compute from public filings, and the Sept 1 sell-off shows the market traded the pro forma. So a guide near the arithmetic is roughly what the price holds, though headlines will call it a cut from $70-73M. Q3 revenue will look like a miss against a stale $254M consensus: my estimate is about $237M from $265.1M a year ago, comps and roughly 5 weeks of the sold stores' revenue removed. That is optics, not information. What can move the price is outside the arithmetic. Upside: a G&A cut sized to the smaller company base (the pro forma left G&A at $76M), a FY27 framework, free-cash-flow and interest savings (the old 12% debt was replaced by a $90M term loan at SOFR+325). Downside: Q3 restaurant margin hit by beef inflation (peers cite high-teens beef inflation) and higher marketing spend, traffic getting worse (-1.7% against -0.4%), lease-guarantee contingencies, or a control or accounting finding in the delayed 10-Q. I cannot see which side lands. The 5-day idiosyncratic weakness lowers the bar a little. The activists' exit from the board (JCP 10.3%, Jumana 8.8%, low cost basis, waived replacement seats) is a sell overhang, but it plays out over weeks, not by the next open. Net: close to a coin flip, with a large move either way.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line, the rebuilt FY26 guide, has a mechanical part the market could price from the 2026-09-01 pro forma and visibly did. The discretionary parts (G&A right-sizing, Q3 margin under beef inflation, the 10-Q's lease-guarantee and accounting disclosures) have no dated public input that tilts them. I can show no gap between the price and the evidence large enough to bet on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An updated FY26 adj EBITDA guide clearly above about $60M, or a stated G&A reduction plan, would make me lean up. A guide below about $55M, a Q3 restaurant-level margin under 11%, or a material-weakness or lease-guarantee charge in the 10-Q would make me lean down.

self_critique: Case for up: every 2026 print reaction was large and positive. The stock has given back about 12% since the preliminary release while peers rose, so the bar may be low. Interest savings (from about 12% to about 7.3% on a smaller debt), a likely G&A cut and the comps beat could give a cleaner free-cash-flow story than the market's post-pro-forma pessimism, against roughly 10% short interest. Case for down: the headline guide will read as a cut from $70-73M; with thin coverage, stale consensus and retail holders, it may be read at face value overnight. Traffic is getting worse, beef inflation is high, and a delayed 10-Q tends to carry bad surprises more often than good ones. Both cases are real and neither rests on dated evidence about the discretionary lines, so 49 stands.
approach_notes: P4 helped most: the 'priced in' claim for the refranchising drag was provable from the dated pro forma and the Sept 1 price move, rather than assumed. P6's peer and index run-in split showed the 5-day slide was partly idiosyncratic but tied to no news. The playbook says little about guides reset by M&A or disposals, where a mechanical cut and a real cut look the same in headlines.
